primary_diagnosis: Opioid use disorder with analgesic (NSAID/acetaminophen) nephropathy
clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient presents with uncontrolled stage‑2 hypertension, obesity, prediabetes, and untreated OSA, forming a classic metabolic‑syndrome picture. Laboratory data reveal early CKD (elevated creatinine, metabolic acidosis, borderline hyper‑kalemia) and reactive thrombocytosis. A long history of opioid dependence with multiple overdoses and frequent pain‑related ED visits, combined with the absence of documented analgesic prescriptions, strongly suggests chronic use of nephrotoxic analgesics contributing to the renal impairment. These factors together explain the resistant hypertension and metabolic derangements. Secondary contributors include possible secondary hypertension, chronic viral infection risk, and psychosocial stressors that may underlie undocumented depression and poor adherence. Low‑normal leukocyte count and normal lipid profile despite metabolic syndrome remain unexplained, highlighting data gaps.

HIV antigen/antibody combo and hepatitis C antibody (with RNA if positive)
Iron studies (ferritin, transferrin saturation, TIBC) to assess iron‑deficiency anemia
Repeat fasting lipid panel including triglycerides and LDL‑particle size

Dental evaluation of impacted molars for infection or inflammation
PHQ‑9, GAD‑7, and PTSD screening for mood and anxiety disorders
Vaccination review (influenza, COVID‑19, hepatitis B, HPV) and update as needed
